Unveiling the Therapeutic Potential of Bioactive Phytocompounds from Ficus bengalensis bark in the Epigenetic Regulation of OSCC

Abstract:

Ficus benghalensis (Banyan tree) is widely recognised for its rich phytochemistry and therapeutic potential. The present study explored the metabolite profile and anticancer efficacy of the methanolic extract of F. benghalensis bark (MEFB) and its key bioactive flavone in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). MEFB was prepared by maceration and subjected to qualitative and quantitative phytochemical screening, metabolite profiling by GC-MS and LC-MS (ESI positive and negative modes), and structural characterisation by ATR-FTIR and ¹H NMR spectroscopy. Molecular docking against epigenetic modifiers revealed strong interaction of the flavone subclass with DNMT1 and HDAC1. The extract showed significant antioxidant activity (DPPH IC₅₀, 22.95 μg/mL). In vitro, MEFB and the flavone markedly inhibited OSCC cell proliferation, migration and clonogenic potential. Mechanistically, flavone treatment caused dose-dependent downregulation of DNMT1 and HDAC1, reversal of epithelial mesenchymal transition with increased CDH1 (E-cadherin) and decreased Vimentin expression, suppression of cancer stemness markers, and inhibition of RAS-MAPK signalling. Combination with the DNMT1 inhibitor azacytidine enhanced efficacy, producing more pronounced DNMT1 suppression and synergistic CDH1 upregulation than either agent alone. These findings identify the flavone as a key driver of the anticancer activity of MEFB and a promising multi-targeted candidate for oral cancer management.
